title: Protocol assurance ladder
question: Is the protocol well built, well tested, and safe to run?
principle: Assurance is about structure, testing, and safety. It says nothing about whether the protocol improves anyone's work. A protocol can reach the top of this ladder and still make its users slower — that is the other ladder's job to detect. One badge must never stand for both. Every rung means only what its check actually established: an offline check of the shipped examples is not the same as a live run of the protocol, and the rung names say so.

states.label: Draft
states.meaning: The procedure exists but has not passed its own checks.

states.label: Structure validated
states.meaning: Schema- and structure-valid: required fields present, enums and patterns satisfied, kernel steps mapped, and the file inventory matches the manifest. This is a check of the DOCUMENT, not of the protocol's behaviour or its semantic fidelity to the kernel.
states.established_by: tools/validate.js passes against protocol.schema.json and the structural kernel checks; MANIFEST.json matches the files on disk.

states.label: Example conformance validated
states.meaning: The worked examples SHIPPED IN THE PACK satisfy the acceptance tests under deterministic graders, and deliberately-bad fixtures are rejected by those graders (discrimination). This proves the acceptance tests are mechanised and discriminating against the pack's own examples. It does NOT run a model over a fresh task, observe real actions, or establish that a model executing the protocol would conform.
states.established_by: tools/eval-harness.js --tests passes, including discrimination cases, and evals designs are valid.
states.gate: example fixtures + graders (offline, no model execution)

states.label: Task set passed
states.meaning: A live runner executed the protocol over the registered task set on at least one named model/runtime, and the FRESH outputs — not hand-authored fixtures — passed the acceptance tests, with observed actions rather than self-reported receipts. The offline harness cannot grant this; it requires a real run.
states.established_by: A recorded live run over the task set whose captured outputs pass the acceptance tests, bound by hashes to task, output, grader, runner, and protocol version.
states.gate: live run over the task set

states.label: Cross-model reproduced
states.meaning: A separate model or implementation obtains materially consistent results on the task set in live runs.
states.established_by: The task set is run under at least two distinct models/runtimes and the acceptance-test outcomes agree.

states.label: Security reviewed
states.meaning: Permissions, external calls, and hostile-input behaviour have been inspected by a human, the static scan is clean, and any runtime enforcement path (sandbox, capability mediation) has been considered. The static scanner alone does not grant this.
states.established_by: tools/hostile-tests.js passes AND a human security review of scripts, adapters, and declared permissions is recorded.

states.label: Field ready
states.meaning: Suitable for bounded real-world trials by people outside the development team. Requires a live-run history (>= TASKSET_PASSED), a security review, a copy-and-run edition, and no open critical defect. Blocked while productivity evidence is HARM_OR_REGRESSION_FOUND.
states.established_by: All lower gates plus a copy-and-run edition, install instructions, live-run history, and no open critical failure.

states.label: Deprecated
states.meaning: No longer recommended. Kept for the record, withdrawn from active use.
states.established_by: A maintainer decision, a security withdrawal, or a retest trigger that the protocol no longer survives.
